ns2:course.label: Macroeconomic Theory II
ns2:course.description: Development of modern macroeconomic theory, including disequilibrium theory, optimal short-term stabilization measures, and monetary, fiscal, incomes, and exchange rate policies; large-scale econometric models; linear and neoclassical growth models; aggregate distribution theory; money, capital movements, trade, and growth; optimal growth models; and exhaustible resources and growth. Prerequisite: ECON 531.
ns2:course.sectionDeptRestriction: Restricted to students in the Economics department.
